title: fix(runtime,objectql): ctx.title() answers a title formula over lookups — the one hop is served on the body's own channel
body:
Part of #24197 (part 2 of 3: the hook-body title accessor. The ADR-0079 note follows as its own Tier H PR.)

Clause-②: yes (widening) (re-declared by the seat in claim 6249052664: the `@objectstack/objectql` index gains `resolveServedRecordTitle`, `servedRecordTitle` and the type `FormulaServingChannel`, and the exported classes `ObjectQL` and `ScopedContext` each gain a public `serveFormulaField`; nothing is removed or renamed. The accessor's own answer is a declared capability honoured: it names the record by its declared title.)

**Published export change, reported for the seat to re-declare the line above:** `@objectstack/objectql`'s `index.ts` gains `resolveServedRecordTitle`, `servedRecordTitle` and the type `FormulaServingChannel`. The exported classes `ObjectQL` and `ScopedContext` each gain one public method, `serveFormulaField`. Nothing is removed or renamed. The changeset grades objectql `minor` and runtime `patch`.

## What was wrong

PR #24274 made the read path serve one hop, so `GET` of a junction object shows `record.book.title + ' · ' + record.reader.name`. A hook body's `ctx.title()` still answered `null` for it. Both forms of the accessor evaluated the title with the synchronous `evaluateFormulaField`, which preloads no hop. `ctx.title('field')` also discarded the related record's own one-hop title that its `findOne` had already served, because it re-derived the title synchronously.

## What changed

- **`ObjectQL.serveFormulaField(objectName, record, field, context)`** (`engine.ts`) evaluates one declared formula field over a record in hand, the way a read evaluates it. It uses the same plan builder, the same hop loader (`resolveFormulaRelated` → `resolveOneHopRelated(…, 'caller')`, including the `formulaHopReads` one-hop guard), the same `can()` permission map and the same fault sink. No second loader or evaluator is added anywhere, and runtime has no copy of either.
- **`ScopedContext.serveFormulaField(objectName, record, field)`** calls it with the context's own `ExecutionContext`. That is the body's `ctx.api` channel, so its identity, its permissions and (inside a transaction) its `transaction` handle all carry over.
- **`record-title.ts`** adds `resolveServedRecordTitle(schema, record, channel)`, the async sibling of `resolveRecordTitle`. It also adds `servedRecordTitle(schema, row)`, which reads the title a read already served off the row. `resolveRecordTitle` is unchanged and still serves no hop. Its docblock now says so.
- **`body-runner.ts` `buildTitleSurface`:**
  - `ctx.title()` resolves over `hookRecordState` (the in-flight state) on the channel the installer hands in per call (`txState.api ?? ctx.api`).
  - `ctx.title('field')` reads the title off the row its `findOne` served.
  - A channel without `serveFormulaField` falls back to the synchronous path, which still resolves a title over the record's own columns. That is the unscoped api of a `runAs: 'user'` hook with no user, which cannot read.

**Which channel serves the hop, and why.** The body's own `ctx.api`, transaction-scoped when the body has one open. The hop is the engine's own loader (`this.find` on the target with the channel's context). It is not a repository read through the channel's `object(...)`, because a repository rebuilds the query object, which would lose the identity-keyed one-hop marker and let the related object's formulas take a second hop.

## Hypotheses, measured

| | Hypothesis | Result |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | `ctx.title()` follows the in-flight key | **Confirmed.** `beforeInsert` names the payload's book. A `beforeUpdate` that moves `book` b1 to b2 names `Emma`, not `Dune`. `afterUpdate` names the after-state. |
| H2 | The hop rides the body's channel | **Confirmed on real SQLite** (better-sqlite3, one pooled connection). In a `beforeUpdate` where the body opens `ctx.api.transaction` (the body owns it), both hop reads run on that transaction's handle. In an `afterUpdate`, the body JOINS the write's own unit of work (`inAfterAbortUnit`), and every read runs on that one handle. Ablation: when the hop is routed through the hook's base `api` instead, the owned-transaction pin hangs (`Acquire connection error: aborted`, test timeout at 30 s), which is the deadlock. |
| H3 | Re-deriving the related title discards a served one-hop value | **Confirmed.** With the old re-derivation, `ctx.title('book')` for a book whose title is `record.title + ' @ ' + record.shelf.code` answers `null`. Reading the served value answers `Dune @ A-1`, which equals `findOne` for the same caller. |
| H4 | A caller who may not read a related record gets the read's answer | **Confirmed.** Row-level security hides one reader. `ctx.title()` answers `null`, and `findOne` of the junction row as the same caller answers `title: null`. Neither returns the readable half or the hidden name. SYSTEM gets `Dune · Hidden Person` from both (control). |
| H5 | No second hop | **Confirmed.** A copy titled `record.book.label`, where the book's `label` reads its shelf, answers `null` from both `ctx.title()` and the read. No `lib_shelf` read is issued. |

**Cost (measured):** a title over lookups costs one batched read per reference field it reads through: exactly +2 reads (`lib_book`, `lib_reader`) against the same write with a body that does not ask, and the book read is `where id $in [b1]` with fields `[id, title]`. A title over the row's own columns still costs 0 reads; that pin is kept and renamed to say so. The related form costs one `findOne`, plus whatever hop that record's own title formula reads.

## Verification

Head `0d133459d7` (after merging `origin/main`):
- **Full build:** `pnpm build --concurrency=2`, 76/76 tasks, exit 0.
- **Typecheck:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/{objectql,runtime,cli} typecheck` exit 0 each. Each script includes `check:test-typecheck` over `tsconfig.test.json`, so the new tests are type-checked.
- **Suites:**
  - `@objectstack/objectql` `pnpm test`: 439 files, 8280 tests passed.
  - `@objectstack/runtime` `pnpm test`: 418 files, 6574 passed and 19 skipped, run on the pre-merge head `650581b9`.
  - On the final head, rebuilt: `hook-ctx-title-one-hop.integration.test.ts` and `hook-ctx-title.integration.test.ts` 20/20, and `engine-formula-one-hop.test.ts` and `record-title.test.ts` 47/47.
- **New pins:**
  - `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/hook-ctx-title-one-hop.integration.test.ts`: 11 tests (real engine, real SQLite, real QuickJS).
  - 8 tests in `engine-formula-one-hop.test.ts`, covering `serveFormulaField`: hop by the in-hand key, parity with `findOne`, zero reads for own columns, the transaction handle, the caller-permission null, no second hop, and the served row title.
- **Gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no paths) derived 102 commands. All 102 ran, each exit captured before any pipe: 102 × exit 0. `--ran` output: "102 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 102 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED".
- **Ablations:** made via `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. Each one landed (anchor 1 → 0, blob moved), and each restore was proven by blob == HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty.
  - **A1:** served path → synchronous `resolveRecordTitle`. 8 of the 11 runtime pins go red.
  - **A2:** channel → the hook's base `api`. The owned-transaction H2 pin deadlocks and times out.
  - **A3:** related form re-derives. The H3 pin goes red (`null`).
  - **A4:** engine hop read as SYSTEM. Exactly the caller-permission pin goes red.
  - **A5:** `ScopedContext` drops `transaction`. Exactly the transaction pin goes red.
  - A4 and A5 ran on the objectql suite, which imports `./engine.js` from source, so no `dist` leg was needed. A1 to A3 mutate runtime source, which that suite imports directly.

## Settled choices (see the report's open questions)

- **The related form prefers the served value.** It no longer re-derives. The old guard defended against a hypothetical embedder whose `findOne` does not compute formulas. Every in-repo channel (`ScopedContext`, `ql.object`, `ql.createContext`, the repo facade over `ql.find`) computes them. Re-deriving also computed a title that field-level security had deleted from the row.
- **`ctx.title()` still needs no capability**, even when the title's hop reads. The hop reads are the declaration's, made on the body's own channel under the caller's permissions. Requiring `api.read` only when a title happens to traverse a lookup would make a body's grant depend on another object's metadata.

## Deviations from the claim's file surface

These are comment-only or documentation-only edits outside the fence. The pin sweep forced each one, because each stated the old cost:
- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`: three rows and one bullet pair said `ctx.title()` performs no read.
- `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts` and `script-runner.ts`: comments and a docblock.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/extract-hook-body.ts`: one comment.

No behaviour changed in any of them. The two existing measurement pins in `hook-ctx-title.integration.test.ts` keep their assertions and are renamed to the own-column case.

## Acceptance notes

- **REST parity is pinned against `engine.findOne` with the same context.** That is the read the REST data route serves. No HTTP server was booted.
- **A hop's target in the stored-metadata family is not refused for a body's title.** The hop is the engine's read, so it does not pass through the body api's family-read refusal (`refuseStoredMetadataBodyReads`). It is still read under the caller's own permissions, and the REST read serves the same value. No in-repo object composes a title through a lookup to a family table. Noted here, not filed.
- **The changelog text of #11293 (`packages/*/CHANGELOG.md`) still says "no read at all".** That text is release-owned, so it is left as is. This PR's changesets state the new cost.
